rationale: The Court is likely to reverse in a Roberts opinion applying Din/Mandel to hold that citing a valid INA inadmissibility ground satisfies the “facially legitimate and bona fide” standard absent a plausible, particularized bad-faith allegation, while avoiding a definitive ruling on the existence or scope of any citizen-spouse liberty interest. Separate writings are most likely from Thomas (to emphasize plenary-power/separation-of-powers limits) and from Sotomayor (possibly with Jackson) to argue that § 1182(a)(3)(A)(ii) is too open-textured for a bare citation to be meaningfully reviewable.
